purpose: Test-or-retire for LMCache: the one real user corruption report (cosmicnag, context edition discussion #1) has LMCache 0.5.2 kv_both disk reuse at chunk 1600 as its sole surviving suspect after receipts/apc-poison-repro.json (266 scored requests, NOT REPRODUCED without LMCache) and receipts/second-5090-datapoint.json (prefix caching + align clean at the native window on a second physical 5090, LMCache disabled) eliminated every other member of his decisive control. arms.L0: control: promoted image, reporter profile, glm52-lmcache-wrapper.sh with LMCACHE_MODE=off (the wrapper execs the model server untouched). Fresh server, 38 requests.
arms.L1cold: LMCache kv_both disk, EMPTY L2 (directory wiped, recorded): fresh server, 38 requests. Cold pass: every chunk is stored, nothing can be retrieved from a prior life.
arms.L2warm: the SAME live server immediately after L1cold, 38 requests again. Warm pass: vLLM's own prefix cache and LMCache L1/L2 are all live; whichever layer serves the hit is recorded from the counters, not assumed.
arms.L3restart: full server stop, then a NEW server over the RETAINED L2 directory, 38 requests. Restart pass: vLLM's own prefix cache and LMCache's L1 start empty by construction, so any prefix reuse is LMCache disk retrieval. This is the reuse-after-restart path the reporter's workflow exercised and vLLM's own cache never can, and it is the prime suspect mechanism.

results.headline: LMCache 0.5.2+glm52dcp.4 kv_both disk reuse at chunk 1600 returns wrong KV for the LAST chunk it supplies. A falsifiable rule fixed on needle geometry predicts every bounded failure with zero false negatives across 114 request-arm instances, and the same geometry served by vLLM's own prefix cache is correct 7/7 - so the defect is attributed to the chunk LMCache supplies, not to prefix reuse as such. Reuse after a process restart over a warm disk L2 escalates past the rule to total corruption: 38/38 requests corrupted, SpecDecoding acceptance median 0.0, multilingual token soup with U+FFFD - the reporter's symptom verbatim.

the_predictive_rule_this_is_the_primary_.rule: a request fails if and only if a SCORED needle lies inside the LAST 1600-token chunk supplied by the cache, i.e. inside [hit_tokens - 1600, hit_tokens)
the_predictive_rule_this_is_the_primary_.why_it_is_falsifiable: the needle token offsets are properties of the frozen prompt set (prompts_sha256 9978404b...), fixed before any arm ran; hit_tokens is read from vLLM's own per-request prefix_cache_hits counter delta. Neither quantity is fitted to the outcome. The rule predicts a specific subset of requests and could have been wrong on any of 114 instances.

needle_geometry_used.note: offset = needle token_end in the document + head_tokens; both from the frozen prompts.json staged on aiboss (out/stage.json prompts_sha256)

the_predictive_rule_this_is_the_primary_.scope_of_the_rule: the three bounded arms L0, L1cold, L2warm = 114 request-arm instances. L3restart is OUTSIDE the rule's scope and is reported separately below; that is a bound on the rule, not a hole in it.
the_predictive_rule_this_is_the_primary_.zero_false_negatives: predicted_pass_but_failed = 0. Every single failure observed in L1cold and L2warm is predicted by the rule.

the_seven_predicted_fail_but_passed_are_.what_they_are: all 7 are in L0, the no-LMCache control, at the IDENTICAL geometry: a scored needle inside the last reused 1600-token chunk, same needle offsets, same hit-token boundaries
the_seven_predicted_fail_but_passed_are_.why_this_is_attribution_not_correlation: the geometry is held fixed and the only thing that differs is which component supplied that final chunk. Supplied by vLLM's own prefix cache: 7/7 correct. Supplied by LMCache: 14/14 wrong. The delta chunk LMCache supplies is what carries wrong KV.

signature_1_wrong_needle.observed: A1 returns needle N03's code 0E4E87AD (record 00054) instead of N01's 90E1F14D (record 00018); A3 then reports '00054,00054'
signature_1_wrong_needle.token_evidence: fires at exactly 1600 hit tokens = one LMCache chunk, whose span [0,1600) contains N01 at prompt offset 926
signature_1_wrong_needle.instances: p2s1, p3s1, p4s1 in both LMCache arms; p1s2 in L1cold; p1s1 in L2warm
signature_1_wrong_needle.control: the same requests at 0 hit tokens in L0 are correct, and p1s3/p2s3/p3s2/p4s2/p4s3 in L0 sit at exactly 1600 hit tokens with N01 in that same last chunk and are correct

signature_2_needle_vanishes.token_evidence: fires at 6400 hit tokens where L0 was correct at 4800 - one extra 1600-token chunk. The extra chunk spans [4800,6400) and contains N07 at prompt offset 5725
signature_2_needle_vanishes.instances: p1s5, p2s5, p3s4 in both LMCache arms
signature_2_needle_vanishes.control: the same three requests in L0 took 4800 hit tokens, leaving N07's chunk to be recomputed, and answered correctly

the_two_signatures_are_one_mechanism_see.unification: in both signatures the corrupted content is the needle that lives in the final chunk LMCache supplied. Earlier LMCache-supplied chunks in the same request are fine: requests at 3200 or 4800 hit tokens whose scored needles fall in earlier chunks pass. p1s2 shows this within one request - wrong at 1600 hit tokens in L1cold with N01 in the last chunk, correct at 4800 hit tokens in L2warm with N01 no longer in the last chunk.

l3restart_escalation.why_it_exceeds_the_rule: in L1cold and L2warm the damage is confined to the last LMCache-supplied chunk. In L3restart it is not.

the_p1s1_caveat_stated_as_a_bound_on_sco.observation: p1s1 in L3restart took 0 hit tokens - LMCache retrieved nothing for it - and still returned the signature-1 wrong needle (A1=0E4E87AD, A3=00054,00054)
the_p1s1_caveat_stated_as_a_bound_on_sco.reading: once the restart pass is under way the damage is no longer confined to reused chunks: 31 of the 38 failures are outside anything the chunk rule predicts, and one of them took no reused tokens at all. That is why this arm is 38/38 rather than 7/38. Stated as a bound on the rule's scope, not as a hole in it: the rule describes the bounded single-process arms, and the restart arm is a strictly worse regime that the rule does not attempt to cover.
the_p1s1_caveat_stated_as_a_bound_on_sco.not_claimed: this receipt does NOT claim a mechanism for the restart-arm blowup beyond the measurement. Whether bad state loaded from disk contaminates the shared hybrid-mamba cache for co-resident requests was not instrumented and is not asserted.

LMCache/LMCache#2206.title: [BUG] Incorrect output when LMCache loads partial chunks overlapping with vLLM prefix cache
LMCache/LMCache#2206.relevance: independently proposed, in December 2025, the mechanism our rule measures: when the vLLM-cached token count is not chunk-aligned, a single chunk ends up mixing vLLM's live KV with LMCache's stored KV, and attention over that mixed chunk is inconsistent. Our result is a quantitative version of that hypothesis - the failure localises to the LAST chunk supplied, with zero false negatives over 114 request-arm instances and a same-geometry control that is correct 7/7 without LMCache. Recorded here because the issue is closed and the hypothesis in it was never confirmed with a control.
